newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts man fined for letting pet cobra loose.
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts man fined for letting pet cobra loose.

text.p: A Massachusetts man who accidentally let his snake out of the bag in a Boston suburb was sentenced to two years probation and fined $5,000 on Wednesday.

Anthony Ferrari, 33, of Stoneham, Mass. owned a venomous Egyptian cobra that got loose in August and caused an uproar in the town. The snake was found alive in November hiding in the closet of a fourth-grade classroom at the local school.

"It's lucky that a child wasn't bitten by this snake. I strongly advise anyone looking for a new pet to stick to a cat or dog, or at least anything that isn't poisonous," U.S. Attorney for Massachusetts Donald Stern said.
Ferrari pleaded guilty to violating federal wildlife protection laws, a misdemeanor.
The man who allegedly sold Ferrari the snake, David McKinney, 22, of Montevallo, Alabama, was scheduled to appear in Birmingham, Ala. for a federal court hearing on Thursday.
